1.explanation: Each of these files defines the skeleton version of its respective form component and emits an empty <label> element to preserve layout.  Because the label has no text or accessible name, automated DAP checks report a violation.  To fix the issue, each skeleton file must include either visible placeholder text or a hidden accessible name (e.g. via aria-label or visually-hidden content) so that the label element is not empty.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the “skeleton” (loading placeholder) variants of all form controls—Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, Slider, TextArea and TextInput—the generated <label> elements are completely empty (no inner text or aria-label) which triggers a DAP accessibility violation “Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements.”  Because the skeleton code emits <label class="bx--label bx--skeleton" htmlFor="…"></label> with no child text or accessible name, screen readers cannot identify the associated input or placeholder.

2.explanation: Each of these files contains the implementation of the “skeleton” (placeholder) state for its respective input component. They all render a <label> element with the Carbon skeleton styling but leave the label content blank. Because <label> elements must include descriptive text (or an accessible alternative) to identify the associated form control, having them empty causes a DAP accessibility violation. Fixing these files (for example by adding visually hidden text or aria-label attributes) will resolve the missing-label issue.
2.bug_scenario: When viewing the Carbon React skeleton variants for Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, Slider, TextArea, and TextInput, each skeleton component renders an empty <label> (with the skeleton CSS classes) but no inner text. Running IBM DAP against these pages reports a violation “Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements” because the label has no text that identifies the expected input.
